text.p: The charitable foundation that owns Italian savings bank Cariplo said it had given its formal approval to the planned merger with Banco Ambrosiano Veneto.

The foundation of the Milan-based Cassa di Risparmio delle Provincie Lombarde said in a statement that after the operation it would hold 29 percent of the capital of the parent which will control Cariplo and Ambroveneto.
This holding would be reduced to 22 percent over the next five years, it added.
The foundation also said it would purchase the 12.62 percent stake held by Cassa di Risparmio di Verona in Ambroveneto at a price of 7,190 lire per share for a total of 455.3 billion lire.
This stake will be integrated with the purchase of other minority holdings in Ambroveneto to give the foundation an initial stake of 16 percent, the statement said.
To bring its holding to 29 percent, the foundation will participate in Ambroveneto's planned capital increase.
Ambroveneto's board has already approved the move to boost its capital by up to 6.8 trillion lire over five years in preparation for the takeover of 100 percent of the banking assets of Cariplo.
